title: rotation-playbook-skills-matrix-and-postmortem-rubric-2024
author: Leah Ortega
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the on-call skills matrix, evidence-collection templates, postmortem rubric, and repeatable game-day scenarios used by Redwood Inference responders. It is intended for SREs, service owners, and engineers who rotate on the primary/secondary on-call schedule. The document complements per-service runbooks (see related pages) and standard incident process docs.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-ack and time-to-repair for production incidents.
- Standardize evidence collection to make postmortems faster and more actionable.
- Provide an objective rubric for postmortem severity, RCA depth, and follow-up actions.
- Provide a repeatable rotational training syllabus (game days and shadowing).

Scope
- Applies to all customer-facing inference services: redwood-router, control-plane-api, redwood-serving, batcher, kv-cache, and console.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks; it provides a canonical structure for on-call competency and forensics.

Quick links (operational)
- Datadog: queries to attach to alerts (copy/paste)
  - latency_95p_by_service: "avg(last_5m):p95:trace.redwood.*{env:prod,service:*} > 300"
  - error_rate_5m: "sum(last_5m):errors{service:redwood-serving} / sum(last_5m):requests{service:redwood-serving} > 0.02"
- Kibana saved search: "redwood_errors_primary" (logs w/ trace_id, request_id, model, shard_id)
- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/YYYY-MM/<<incident-id>>

Rotation and Handoff
1. Rotation cadence
   - Primary: 1 week (Mon 08:00 UTC — next Mon 08:00 UTC)
   - Secondary: 1 week, same cadence, different roster
   - On-call lead: monthly assignment; responsible for triage quality and postmortem orchestration
2. Handoff checklist (required before leaving shift)
   - Confirm no ongoing SevP incidents assigned to you; if there are, ensure active owner and next steps are documented.
   - Run the oncall-summary script: `./scripts/oncall-summary --service redwood-serving --since 4h` and paste results into the handoff note.
   - Verify that runbook pages you touched are linked in the handoff (service-runbook, postmortem draft).
   - Shadowing requirement: new primaries must have two full handoffs under supervision before unsupervised primary.
3. Escalation contact matrix (primary responsibility)
   - Primary responder -> Secondary after 15m of progress-blocked with customer impact or no mitigation
   - Secondary -> On-call lead after 30m of unresolved SevP or urgent compliance/regulatory impact

Skills Matrix (competency levels)
Columns: Skill area | Level 1 (observer) | Level 2 (contributor) | Level 3 (owner) | Level 4 (expert)
- Basic triage: read service health dashboards, identify impacted clusters
  - L1: can read console dashboard and find the service tile
  - L2: can interpret p95/p99 trends and correlate with deployment events
  - L3: can identify root symptom (e.g., KV eviction spike) and propose mitigation
  - L4: can implement and test mitigation in prod-like environment and mentor others
- Forensics & evidence collection:
  - L1: copy paste error logs and request ids to a doc
  - L2: collect traces, flamegraphs, and shard mappings into evidence bucket
  - L3: run KV cache dump and rehydrate small sample; produce minimal repro
  - L4: author scripts to automate evidence collection for the service
- Communications & stakeholder updates:
  - L1: post basic status updates using templates
  - L2: manage staged status page messages and coordinate with CSR
  - L3: author press-ready customer notices and lead bridge calls
  - L4: lead cross-org exec briefings and regulatory notifications

Training syllabus (onboarding & ongoing)
- Week 0 (shadowing): observe two full incidents and two handoffs, complete evidence-collection checklist twice.
- Month 1 (supervised primary): lead 1 low-severity incident, co-lead 1 game day.
- Quarterly: participate in at least one game day (see scenarios) and one postmortem writeup.
- Annual: take the responder proficiency assessment (practical exercise + quiz).

Evidence collection template (required artifacts)
- Minimal artifact set (attach to postmortem and incident ticket):
  - Incident timeline (UTC): high-level bullets of detection -> mitigation -> recovery
  - Alert firing time, summary alert query, and thresholds
  - Top 5 Datadog graphs (embed links): latency, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, KV eviction rate
  - Representative logs (10–50 lines) with trace_id and request_id; include noise-filtering criteria used
  - Distributed trace(s) (link to trace viewer) showing end-to-end latency and spans with high duration
  - Snapshot of deployment events (k8s events, rolling update timestamps, AMI/driver changes)
  - Evidence storage path: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/YYYY-MM/INCIDENT-<id>/

Forensic commands (examples)
- Capture top kernels / GPU usage (run by infra only): `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1`
- Dump Redis / KV cache top keys: `redis-cli --rdb /tmp/dump.rdb && aws s3 cp /tmp/dump.rdb s3://redwood-incident-evidence/...`
- Trace sampler: `curl -sS -X POST "https://control-plane-api.prod/redwood/trace/sample" -d '{"request_id":"<id>"}'`

Incident process: step-by-step
1. Detect & Triage
   - Owner: whoever acknowledges the alert (Primary)
   - Actions: acknowledge in PagerDuty, post start time in incident ticket, run initial triage checklist (see runbook fragment below).
2. Classify impact (immediately)
   - Severity definitions (use these precisely):
     - SevP (Production outage): >10% of customer requests failing OR API availability < 95% for 5m; requires bridge within 15m.
     - SevA (Major degradation): 2–10% customer impact or p95 latency > 800ms for 5m; bridge within 30m if not immediately mitigated.
     - SevB (Degradation): transient spikes or single-region issues, customer impact <2%; handled on primary with async update.
     - SevC (Informational): non-customer-impacting issues (errors in background jobs, telemetry issues).
3. Mitigate & Stabilize
   - Tactics: circuit-break, rollout rollback, regional failover, scale up replica count, enable degraded-mode cache bypass.
   - Owner: service owner or SRE on-call with escalation to infra for capacity changes.
4. Communicate
   - Post initial status to status.redwood.ai and in the incident ticket within 15 minutes for SevP/SevA.
   - Use staged templates below.
5. Recover & Validate
   - Run validation checklist (smoke tests, synthetic traffic, targeted trace checks).
6. Close incident and submit preliminary postmortem within 72 hours for SevP/A; within 7 days for SevB.

Runbook fragment (initial triage checklist)
1. Identify impact: which service, region(s), % of traffic affected, customer segments (enterprise, dedi, private).
2. Attach top-5 evidence graphs.
3. Check recent deploys: `kubectl get events --since=1h --all-namespaces` and CI deploy tags.
4. Check capacity & throttling: router token queue length, batcher backlog, GPU utilization.
5. If degraded due to KV cache evictions: attempt `kv-cache flush --shard <id> --grace 30s` and monitor.

Postmortem rubric (grading & expectations)
- Required for SevP/SevA: public postmortem (internal distribution + customer-facing summary)
- Postmortem sections (must be present): title, incident timeline, impact statement, detection root cause, contributing factors, mitigations, follow-up action items (owner + due date), lessons learned
- Severity-to-depth mapping:
  - SevP: Full RCA with root cause analysis (5 Whys + causal tree), quantitative impact analysis (tokens lost, requests failed), and executive summary. Due: preliminary 72h, final 14 days.
  - SevA: Medium RCA with timeline and 3 corrective actions. Due: preliminary 72h, final 10 days.
  - SevB/C: Lightweight postmortem or incident log entry; corrective actions documented if relevant. Due: 7 days.
- Action item SLAs: classify each follow-up as P0/P1/P2 with a target completion window and automated tracking in JIRA.

Customer communications: staged templates (copy/paste)
- Initial (investigating) — short, public status page message
  "We are investigating increased errors/latency impacting some inference requests in US-west. Our engineering team is investigating. We will provide an update within 15 minutes. Impact: some requests may fail or take longer than expected."
- Update (mitigation in progress)
  "Mitigation in progress: we have identified a regression in the kv-cache eviction logic and are applying a local bypass to affected nodes. Expected recovery: ~15–30 minutes. We will update when the service is restored or if timelines change."
- Customer-facing RCA summary (post-incident)
  "On <date> between <start> and <end> UTC, customers experienced elevated errors and increased latency for inference requests due to an unexpected interaction between kv-cache eviction and our autoscaler. We mitigated the issue by disabling eviction on affected shards and performing a controlled scale-up. Root cause: change X in release Y increased average memory pressure and triggered aggressive eviction. Follow-ups: 1) tuning autoscaler thresholds (owner: infra-team, due: 2025-03-15), 2) add canary to eviction change (owner: serving-team, due: 2025-02-28)."

Game-day scenarios (quarterly practice)
- Scenario A: Multi-region failover — simulate primary region outage and exercise cross-region routing and user state preservation.
- Scenario B: KV cache storm — inject high eviction rates and exercise bypass + controlled cache warmup.
- Scenario C: GPU driver regression — simulate degraded kernel performance and practice rolling-back driver and kernel modules.
- Scenario D: Silent SLO regression — synthetic traffic shows p95 increase without obvious errors; objective is evidence collection & RCA within 90 minutes.

Game-day run template
1. Goals & success criteria (set before start).
2. Injected fault & detection signal (who triggers, how).
3. Roles: incident commander, communications lead, service owner, infra lead, observer(s).
4. Timeline: minutes 0–15 triage & classify, 15–45 mitigation plan, 45–90 execute mitigation and validate, 90–120 debrief.
5. Observers score using the skills matrix and provide written feedback.

Post-event debrief & continuous improvement
- Debrief within 48 hours: 30–60 minute meeting with participants and observers. Capture: what went well, what didn't, action items.
- Update runbooks and the skills matrix with observed gaps; owners to close action items and update training curriculum.
- Archive artifacts (recordings, logs, JIRA tasks) under the incident evidence path and tag with game-day-<YYYY-MM>.

Governance & responsibilities
- On-call lead: ensure rotation coverage and that postmortems meet rubric quality.
- Service owners: own mitigations and corrective actions for their services.
- Infra: capacity changes, kernel/driver rollbacks, hardware investigation.
- Customer Success: escalate customer notices for enterprise customers and provide tailored updates.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Sample postmortem timeline template (copy into page)
  - Detection: 2025-02-01T14:03:12Z - Datadog alert fired for p95 latency > 800ms
  - Acknowledge: 14:04:01Z - Primary acknowledged in PagerDuty
  - Bridge formed: 14:15:00Z - Bridge URL: https://zoom/bridge/12345
  - Mitigation decision: 14:40:00Z - roll back canary to v3.2.1
  - Recovery: 15:02:33Z - metrics returned to baseline

- Appendix B: Example evidence folder layout
  - s3://redwood-incident-evidence/2025-02/INC-2025-0021/
  - /artifacts/graphs.png
  - /traces/trace-<id>.json
  - /logs/filtered-log-<id>.log
  - /postmortem/draft.md

Contact & escalation list (primary oncall first)
- PagerDuty: primary-oncall@redwood.ai
- Oncall lead: samir.patel@redwood.ai
- Infra pager: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
- Customer Success: cs-incident@redwood.ai

Document maintenance
- Owner: engineering (on-call lead)
- Review cadence: annually or after any SevP incident; minor updates after every game-day.

Related pages and references
- See service-specific runbooks in the oncall-and-incident-response space.
- For compliance-sensitive incidents, follow security-and-compliance/incident-response-security runbook.

End of document
